questions.q: What is attenuation in the context of medical X-ray imaging?
a: The decrease in intensity of an X-ray beam as it passes through matter due to absorption and scattering
The acceleration of electrons inside an X-ray tube
The amplification of electrical signals in an ultrasound transducer
The bending of gamma rays through magnetic fields

questions.q: How is the linear attenuation coefficient mu defined for an X-ray beam passing through a uniform material of thickness x?
a: I = I_0 * e^(mu * x)
I = I_0 * e^(-mu * x)
I = I_0 - mu * x
I = mu * I_0 / x

questions.q: What is the half-value thickness (HVT) of a material for X-rays?
a: The thickness of material required to reduce the X-ray tube voltage by half
The thickness of material required to double the intensity of an X-ray beam
The thickness of material required to reduce the intensity of an X-ray beam to half its initial value
Half the total physical width of the patient

questions.q: What is the purpose of using a contrast medium (such as barium or iodine compounds) in X-ray imaging?
a: To eliminate all radiation doses to the patient completely
To decrease the energy of the X-ray tube
To speed up the scanning process
To enhance the contrast of soft tissues by greatly increasing X-ray attenuation in specific organs or blood vessels

questions.q: How are X-rays produced in a standard diagnostic X-ray tube?
a: By bombarding a high-melting-point metal target (such as tungsten) with high-speed electrons accelerated through a high potential difference
By spontaneous radioactive decay of cobalt-60
By passing high-frequency alternating current through quartz crystals
By cooling liquid helium to absolute zero

questions.q: What is computed tomography (CT scanning) superior to standard 2D X-ray projection imaging for?
a: Producing zero radiation exposure
Providing detailed 3D cross-sectional images that clearly resolve overlapping soft tissue structures
Cost-free immediate diagnosis
Operating without any electronic detectors

questions.q: What physical principle is utilized in ultrasound imaging transducers?
a: The photoelectric effect
Nuclear magnetic resonance
The piezoelectric effect (converting electrical voltage pulses into mechanical ultrasound vibrations and vice versa)
Electromagnetic induction in rotating coils

questions.q: What is acoustic impedance Z of a medium defined as in ultrasound physics?
a: Z = v / rho
Z = rho / v
Z = rho + v
Z = rho * v (product of density rho and speed of ultrasound in the medium v)

questions.q: Why is a coupling gel applied between the ultrasound transducer and the patient's skin?
a: To match acoustic impedances and prevent almost total reflection of ultrasound waves at the air-skin boundary
To cool down the transducer head
To amplify the electrical current inside the body
To numb the skin during the scan

questions.q: What does the intensity reflection coefficient alpha (or R) depend on when an ultrasound beam travels from medium 1 (impedance Z_1) to medium 2 (impedance Z_2)?
a: The frequency of the ultrasound wave alone
The difference in acoustic impedances: R = ((Z_2 - Z_1) / (Z_2 + Z_1))²
The total thickness of medium 2
The electrical resistance of the skin

questions.q: What is the purpose of Doppler ultrasound in medical diagnostics?
a: To measure bone density
To produce high-resolution images of brain tumors
To measure the speed and direction of blood flow within blood vessels using frequency shifts
To destroy kidney stones non-invasively

questions.q: What is a tracer (radiopharmaceutical) used in Positron Emission Tomography (PET) scanning?
a: A high-powered optical laser beam
A stable, non-radioactive salt solution
An ultrasound gel infused with microbubbles
A biologically active molecule tagged with a positron-emitting radioisotope (such as fluorine-18 in FDG)

questions.q: What fundamental particle interaction occurs when a positron emitted by a PET tracer collides with an electron in the body?
a: Annihilation resulting in the emission of two gamma-ray photons travelling in opposite directions
Elastic scattering producing an alpha particle
Nuclear fusion releasing a neutron
Photoelectric absorption creating an X-ray

questions.q: What is the half-value thickness (HVT) for a material if its linear attenuation coefficient is 0.23 cm⁻¹?
Which medical imaging technique exposes the patient to ionizing radiation?
a: Ultrasound imaging
Standard A-scan and B-scan ultrasonography
Computed Tomography (CT scan)
Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)

questions.q: What is the primary advantage of using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) over CT scanning?
a: It is significantly cheaper and faster
It uses high-intensity X-rays for bone imaging
It requires no specialized cooling systems
It does not use ionizing radiation, offering exceptional soft tissue contrast

questions.q: What role does the strong uniform magnetic field play in an MRI scanner?
a: It aligns the magnetic dipole moments (spin axes) of hydrogen nuclei (protons) in the body
It accelerates electrons to create X-rays
It generates ultrasonic pressure waves
It ionizes tissue molecules for detection

questions.q: What is the function of gradient magnetic coils in an MRI machine?
a: To cool the superconducting magnets to 4 Kelvin
To superimpose small spatial variations on the main magnetic field so different regions of the body can be spatially encoded and localized
To shield the operator room from radio waves
To inject the contrast medium into blood vessels

questions.q: What radiofrequency (RF) pulses are used for in an MRI scan?
a: To cool the patient during the scan
To generate ultrasound echoes
To knock aligned hydrogen protons out of equilibrium, causing them to emit detectable RF signals as they relax back
To accelerate tracer atoms through blood vessels

questions.q: What is the acoustic impedance of muscle tissue, given its density is 1070 kg m⁻³ and the speed of ultrasound in muscle is 1580 m s⁻¹?
a: 1.48 x 10⁶ kg m⁻² s⁻¹
1.69 x 10⁵ kg m⁻² s⁻¹
6.77 x 10² kg m⁻² s⁻¹

questions.q: Why are X-ray tubes evacuated to a high vacuum?
a: To prevent collisions between accelerated electrons and air molecules, which would scatter electrons and lose energy
To allow ultrasound waves to propagate freely
To keep the target metal molten
To generate positrons for PET imaging

questions.q: What is 'sharpness' in X-ray imaging improved by?
a: Using a large physical X-ray source focal spot
Using a small focal spot, placing the patient closer to the image receptor, and using a narrower X-ray beam
Increasing the distance between the X-ray film and the patient indefinitely
Removing all filtration from the X-ray tube

questions.q: What is the purpose of an X-ray filter (such as an aluminum sheet) placed at the tube window?
a: To increase the total radiation dose to the patient's skin
To focus X-rays into a narrow laser beam
To absorb low-energy (soft) X-rays that would otherwise be absorbed by the patient's skin without contributing to the image
To convert X-rays into visible light

questions.q: What is piezoelectric material commonly used in ultrasound probes?
a: Lead zirconate titanate (PZT) ceramic
Pure copper wire coils
Lead shielding blocks
Liquid helium

questions.q: What happens to ultrasound waves when they encounter a boundary between two media with very different acoustic impedances?
a: A large fraction of the ultrasound intensity is reflected at the boundary
All ultrasound waves pass through completely without attenuation
Ultrasound waves convert directly into X-rays
Ultrasound wavelength increases to infinity

questions.q: What is the purpose of the collimator in a gamma camera used for medical scintigraphy?
a: To accelerate radioactive tracers in the bloodstream
To absorb divergent gamma-ray photons and allow only those travelling parallel to the collimator holes to reach the scintillator crystal, forming a sharp image
To filter out high-frequency radio waves
To cool the detector crystal

questions.q: What is the function of the sodium iodide (NaI) scintillator crystal in a gamma camera?
a: To reflect gamma rays back into the patient
To convert gamma-ray photons into high-energy electrons
To absorb incoming gamma-ray photons and re-emit their energy as flashes of visible light photons
To amplify electrical voltage signals electronically

questions.q: What device converts the light flashes from a scintillator crystal into an electrical pulse in a gamma camera or photomultiplier tube assembly?
a: A piezoelectric crystal
An ultrasonic transducer
A high-voltage transformer
A photomultiplier tube (PMT)

questions.q: If the linear attenuation coefficient of bone for 100 keV X-rays is 0.50 cm⁻¹, what percentage of the X-ray beam intensity is transmitted through a 2.0 cm thick bone layer?
a: 50.0 percent
13.5 percent
63.2 percent

questions.q: Why is ultrasound not suitable for imaging structures surrounded by thick bone (such as the adult brain through the skull)?
a: Bones generate high levels of radioactive tracers
High acoustic impedance mismatch and high attenuation coefficient of bone cause severe reflection and absorption of ultrasound waves
Ultrasound travels too fast through bone to be detected
Bones absorb all electrical power from the transducer

questions.q: What is the Doppler frequency shift delta f observed when an ultrasound wave of frequency f reflects off red blood cells moving at velocity v directly towards the transducer (speed of sound in tissue c)?
a: delta f = f * v / c
delta f = 2 * f * v / c
delta f = c / (2 * f * v)
delta f = f * c / v

questions.q: What is the primary biological hazard of ionizing radiation in medical imaging?
a: Thermal burns on the skin surface
Temporary hearing loss
Muscle fatigue during long scans
Ionization of atoms and molecules in living cells, potentially damaging DNA and causing mutations or cancer
